\section{Sawtooth sums and the main term for one modulus}\label{sec:sawtooth}

\subsection{Sawtooth sums}

The function $B(u)=\fr u(1-\fr u)$ is continuous, $1$-periodic, takes values in $[0,\frac14]$, and satisfies $B(u)=u-u^2$ for $0\le u\le1$. The sums we need are $\sum_{s\ge1}B(Z/s^2)$ and weighted versions of them. Their size $\asymp\sqrt Z$ has two sources: the terms with $s>\sqrt Z$, where $B(Z/s^2)=Z/s^2-Z^2/s^4$, and the terms with $s\le\sqrt Z$, where $B$ oscillates. The natural approximation is the integral $\int_0^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du=I\sqrt Z$ (substitute $u=\sqrt Z\,w$). For $q\in\N$ put
\[
\kappa_q(t)=\kappa(t)\one[(t,q)=1],\qquad \Delta_q=\prod_p\Bigl(1-\frac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\one[p\nmid q]\frac{p}{p^2-2}\Bigr).
\]
For $p\nmid q$ the factor of $\Delta_q$ is $(p-1)^2(p+2)/(p(p^2-2))=1+O(p^{-2})$; there are finitely many other factors, so the product converges absolutely.

\begin{proposition}[Sawtooth sums]\label{prop:sawtooth}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item $I=\int_0^\infty B(u^{-2})\,du=\frac12\int_0^\infty B(v)v^{-3/2}\,dv=-4\zeta(-\tfrac12)$.
\item For every real $Z>0$, $\bigl|\sum_{s\ge1}B(Z/s^2)-I\sqrt Z\bigr|\le c_1Z^{1/3}$ with $c_1=60$.
\item For every $\eps>0$ there is $c_5(\eps)$ such that for all $q\in\N$ and real $Z>0$,
\[
\Bigl|\sum_{t\ge1}\kappa_q(t)B(Z/t^2)-\Delta_q\,I\sqrt Z\Bigr|\le c_5(\eps)\,q^\eps Z^{1/3}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(a) The substitution $v=u^{-2}$ gives the second expression. The integral converges, because $B(v)\le v$ near $0$ and $B(v)\le\frac14$. Since $B$ is continuous and piecewise $C^1$ with $B'(v)=1-2\fr v$, integration by parts on $[0,X]$ gives
\[
\int_0^XB(v)v^{-3/2}\,dv=\bigl[-2B(v)v^{-1/2}\bigr]_0^X+2\int_0^XB'(v)v^{-1/2}\,dv .
\]
The boundary term tends to $0$, because $B(v)v^{-1/2}\le v^{1/2}$ near $0$ and $B(X)X^{-1/2}\le\frac14X^{-1/2}$. Hence $\int_0^\infty Bv^{-3/2}\,dv=2\lim_{N\to\infty}\int_0^NB'v^{-1/2}\,dv$ along integers $N$. On $(n,n+1)$ we have $B'(n^+)=1$, $B'((n+1)^-)=-1$ and $B''=-2$, so integrating by parts with the antiderivative $2v^{1/2}$ of $v^{-1/2}$,
\[
\int_n^{n+1}B'(v)v^{-1/2}\,dv=-2(n+1)^{1/2}-2n^{1/2}+4\int_n^{n+1}v^{1/2}\,dv,
\]
and summing over $0\le n<N$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Bprime}
\int_0^NB'(v)v^{-1/2}\,dv=-4\sum_{m=1}^Nm^{1/2}+2N^{1/2}+\tfrac83N^{3/2}.
\end{equation}
Now apply \cref{lem:EM} on $(N,\infty)$ to $G(u)=u^{-s}$ with $\Re s>1$, for which $\sum_{n>N}n^{-s}$ and $\int_N^\infty u^{-s}\,du=N^{1-s}/(s-1)$ converge absolutely, using $\psi(N)=-\frac12$ and $\psi_2(N)=\frac1{12}$:
\[
\sum_{n>N}n^{-s}=\frac{N^{1-s}}{s-1}-\frac{N^{-s}}2+\frac s{12}N^{-s-1}-s(s+1)\int_N^\infty\psi_2(u)u^{-s-2}\,du .
\]
The right-hand side is analytic in $\Re s>-1$, $s\ne1$, because the integral converges locally uniformly there. By uniqueness of analytic continuation, $\zeta(s)=\sum_{n\le N}n^{-s}$ plus the right-hand side in that region. At $s=-\frac12$ we have $s(s+1)=-\frac14$ and $|\int_N^\infty\psi_2u^{-3/2}\,du|\le\frac16N^{-1/2}$, so
\[
\sum_{m\le N}m^{1/2}=\zeta(-\tfrac12)+\tfrac23N^{3/2}+\tfrac12N^{1/2}+O(N^{-1/2}).
\]
Inserting this into~\eqref{eq:Bprime} shows that $\int_0^NB'v^{-1/2}\,dv\to-4\zeta(-\frac12)$. Hence $\int_0^\infty Bv^{-3/2}\,dv=-8\zeta(-\frac12)$ and $I=-4\zeta(-\frac12)$. By the functional equation~\cite[Corollary~10.4]{MV2007} at $s=-\frac12$, $\zeta(-\frac12)=2^{-1/2}\pi^{-3/2}\Gamma(\frac32)\sin(-\frac\pi4)\zeta(\frac32)=-\zeta(\frac32)/(4\pi)$. So $I=\zeta(3/2)/\pi>0$, the value stated in~\eqref{eq:I}.

(b) \emph{The case $Z<1$.} Here $0\le B(Z/s^2)\le Z/s^2$, so $0\le\sum_sB(Z/s^2)\le\zeta(2)Z<2Z^{1/3}$. Also $0<I\sqrt Z<Z^{1/3}$, since $I<1$. The difference of two numbers in $[0,2Z^{1/3}]$ is at most $2Z^{1/3}$.

\emph{The case $Z\ge1$.} Put $\Lambda=Z^{1/3}\ge1$ and $T=\lfloor\Lambda\rfloor\ge1$. Then $\Lambda/2<T\le\Lambda$, hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:b1}
\frac Z{T^3}<8,\qquad K_0:=\frac Z{T^2}<4\Lambda,\qquad \frac{Z^2}{T^5}<32\Lambda .
\end{equation}
\emph{Small $s$.} Both $\sum_{s\le T}B(Z/s^2)$ and $\int_0^TB(Z/u^2)\,du$ lie in $[0,T/4]\subset[0,\Lambda/4]$, so their difference is at most $\Lambda/4$. It therefore suffices to show
\begin{equation}\label{eq:b2}
\Bigl|\sum_{s>T}B(Z/s^2)-\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du\Bigr|\le57\Lambda ,
\end{equation}
which gives the claim with $57+\frac14<60$.

\emph{A decomposition of $B$.} For real $w\ge0$ with $j=\lfloor w\rfloor$ we have $B(w)=(w-j)(1-w+j)=w-w^2+2jw-j-j^2$, and $\sum_{k=1}^j2(w-k)=2jw-j^2-j$. Hence
\[
B(w)=w-w^2+2\sum_{k\ge1}(w-k)_+,\qquad(v)_+=\max(v,0).
\]
Put $\Phi(u)=Z/u^2-Z^2/u^4$ and $G_k(u)=(Z/u^2-k)_+$, so that $B(Z/u^2)=\Phi(u)+2\sum_{k\ge1}G_k(u)$. For $u\ge T$ only the $k<K_0$ contribute, and there are fewer than $K_0<4\Lambda$ of them. For such $k$, $G_k(u)=Z/u^2-k$ on $[T,R_k]$ with $R_k=\sqrt{Z/k}>T$, and $G_k=0$ on $[R_k,\infty)$.

\emph{Euler--Maclaurin.} Apply \cref{lem:EM} to $\Phi$ on $(T,\infty)$ (where $\sum_{s>T}\Phi(s)$ and $\int_T^\infty\Phi$ converge absolutely, since $\Phi(u)=O(u^{-2})$), and to $Z/u^2-k$ on $(T,R_k]$ for each $k<K_0$. Use $\psi(T)=-\frac12$, $\psi_2(T)=\frac1{12}$ and $G_k(R_k)=0$, and add. Since $\int_T^\infty\Phi+2\sum_k\int_T^{R_k}G_k=\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du$ (all integrals converge absolutely), this gives
\[
\sum_{s>T}B(Z/s^2)=\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du+R_1+R_2+R_3+R_4+R_5,
\]
where, writing $G_k'$ and $G_k''$ for the derivatives of $Z/u^2-k$:
\begin{itemize}
\item $R_1=\psi(T)\bigl[\Phi(T)+2\sum_{k<K_0}G_k(T)\bigr]=\psi(T)B(Z/T^2)$. The individual terms here have size about $Z^2/T^4\asymp Z^{2/3}$, but their sum is $B(Z/T^2)\le\frac14$. So $|R_1|\le\frac18$. This is the one place where cancellation is essential.
\item $R_2=-\frac1{12}\bigl[\Phi'(T)+2\sum_{k<K_0}G_k'(T)\bigr]$, with $\Phi'(T)=-2Z/T^3+4Z^2/T^5$ and $G_k'(T)=-2Z/T^3$. By~\eqref{eq:b1}, $|\Phi'(T)|<16+128\Lambda$ and $|2\sum_kG_k'(T)|\le4K_0Z/T^3<128\Lambda$. So $|R_2|\le\frac1{12}(16+256\Lambda)\le\frac{272}{12}\Lambda$.
\item $R_3=-\int_T^\infty\psi_2\Phi''\,du$ with $\Phi''=6Z/u^4-20Z^2/u^6$. So $|R_3|\le\frac1{12}(2Z/T^3+4Z^2/T^5)<\frac1{12}(16+128\Lambda)\le12\Lambda$.
\item $R_4=-2\sum_{k<K_0}\int_T^{R_k}\psi_2G_k''\,du$ with $G_k''=6Z/u^4$ and $\int_T^\infty6Zu^{-4}\,du=2Z/T^3<16$. So $|R_4|\le\frac2{12}K_0\cdot16<\frac{32}3\Lambda$.
\item $R_5=2\sum_{k<K_0}\psi_2(R_k)G_k'(R_k)$ with $G_k'(R_k)=-2Z/R_k^3=-2k^{3/2}/\sqrt Z$. Since $k<4\Lambda$, $\sum_{k<K_0}k^{3/2}<4\Lambda\cdot8\Lambda^{3/2}$, and with $\sqrt Z=\Lambda^{3/2}$ we get $|R_5|\le\frac2{12}\cdot2\cdot32\Lambda=\frac{32}3\Lambda$. These are the kinks of the $G_k$ at the points $R_k$. Summing over the $K_0\asymp Z^{1/3}$ values of $k$ is what produces the exponent $\frac13$.
\end{itemize}
Using $\Lambda\ge1$, the total is at most $(\frac18+\frac{272}{12}+12+\frac{32}3+\frac{32}3)\Lambda=\frac{449}8\Lambda<57\Lambda$, which proves~\eqref{eq:b2}.

(c) Fix $q$. The function $\kappa_q$ is multiplicative with $\kappa_q(p)=p^2/(p^2-2)$ for $p\nmid q$, $\kappa_q(p)=0$ for $p\mid q$ and $\kappa_q(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge2$. Let $\beta=\mu*\kappa_q$, so that $\kappa_q=1*\beta$. Then $\beta$ is multiplicative, with $\beta(p^j)=\kappa_q(p^j)-\kappa_q(p^{j-1})$:
\begin{itemize}
\item for $p\mid q$: $\beta(p)=-1$ and $\beta(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge2$;
\item for $p\nmid q$: $\beta(p)=\frac2{p^2-2}$, $\beta(p^2)=-\frac{p^2}{p^2-2}$ and $\beta(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge3$.
\end{itemize}
\emph{Absolute convergence.} For $p\nmid q$, $\sum_j|\beta(p^j)|p^{-2j/3}\le\frac{2p^{-2/3}}{p^2-2}+2p^{-4/3}$, because $p^2/(p^2-2)\le2$. Hence
\[
\Sigma_{2/3}:=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{|\beta(n)|}{n^{2/3}}\le\prod_{p\mid q}\bigl(1+p^{-2/3}\bigr)\prod_p\Bigl(1+\frac{2p^{-2/3}}{p^2-2}+2p^{-4/3}\Bigr)\le C_\beta\,2^{\omega(q)}\le C_\beta C(\eps)q^\eps,
\]
with an absolute constant $C_\beta$, by \cref{lem:divisor}. Similarly $\sum_n|\beta(n)|/n<\infty$ for each fixed $q$.

\emph{Rearrangement.} For $W>0$, $\sum_mB(W/m^2)\le\sum_m\min(\frac14,W/m^2)\le3\sqrt W$. \[
\sum_{t\ge1}\kappa_q(t)B(Z/t^2)=\sum_{n,m\ge1}\beta(n)B\Bigl(\frac{Z/n^2}{m^2}\Bigr)=\sum_{n\ge1}\beta(n)\sum_{m\ge1}B\Bigl(\frac{Z/n^2}{m^2}\Bigr).
\]
\emph{Main term.} Part (b) holds for every positive argument. Applying it with $Z/n^2$ in place of $Z$, and using $I\sqrt{Z/n^2}=I\sqrt Z/n$,
\[
\Bigl|\sum_t\kappa_q(t)B(Z/t^2)-I\sqrt Z\sum_n\frac{\beta(n)}n\Bigr|\le c_1\sum_n|\beta(n)|\Bigl(\frac Z{n^2}\Bigr)^{1/3}=c_1\Sigma_{2/3}Z^{1/3}.
\]
\emph{The constant.} By~\eqref{eq:euler}, $\sum_n\beta(n)/n=\prod_p\bigl(1+\beta(p)/p+\beta(p^2)/p^2\bigr)$. For $p\mid q$ the factor is $1-1/p$. For $p\nmid q$ it is
\[
1+\frac2{p(p^2-2)}-\frac1{p^2-2}=\frac{p^3-3p+2}{p(p^2-2)}=\frac{(p-1)^2(p+2)}{p(p^2-2)}=\Bigl(1-\frac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\frac p{p^2-2}\Bigr).
\]
Hence $\sum_n\beta(n)/n=\Delta_q$, and (c) holds with $c_5(\eps)=c_1C_\beta C(\eps)$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The main term for one modulus}

\begin{proposition}[Asymptotics of $\MT$]\label{prop:MT}
For every $\eps>0$ there is $c_6(\eps)$ such that for all real $x>0$ and all $q\in\N$,
\[
\bigl|\MT(x;q)-h(q)\sqrt{xq}\bigr|\le c_6(\eps)\,x^{1/3}q^{2/3+\eps},
\]
with $h$ as in~\eqref{eq:h}. In particular this holds for $x\ge1$ and $1\le q\le x$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
\emph{Factorising $t$.} Fix $q$. Every squarefree $t$ factors uniquely as $t=t_0t_1t_2$, where $t_0$ is composed of primes $p\nmid q$, $t_1$ of primes $p\,\|\,q$, and $t_2$ of primes $p$ with $p^2\mid q$. Conversely, every such triple of squarefree numbers gives a squarefree $t$. Let $\mathcal S_1$ and $\mathcal S_2$ be the finite sets of admissible $t_1$ and $t_2$ (all of them divide $q$). For squarefree $t$, $\gcd(t^2,q)=\prod_{p\mid t}p^{\min(2,v_p(q))}=t_1t_2^2$, so
\[
m_t(q)=t_0^2t_1,\qquad\frac x{q\,m_t(q)}=\frac{Z_1}{t_0^2}\quad\text{with}\quad Z_1=\frac{x}{q\,t_1},\qquad \eta(t)m_t(q)=\eta(t_1)\eta(t_2)\,t_1\,\kappa(t_0).
\]
By the absolute convergence in \cref{lem:eta} we may regroup:
\[
\MT(x;q)=A_0\,q\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_1)\eta(t_2)\,t_1\,\Sigma(t_1),\qquad\Sigma(t_1)=\sum_{t_0\ge1}\kappa_q(t_0)B\Bigl(\frac{Z_1}{t_0^2}\Bigr).
\]
\emph{Applying \cref{prop:sawtooth}(c).} With $Z=Z_1>0$ we get $\Sigma(t_1)=\Delta_qI\sqrt{Z_1}+\theta\,c_5(\eps)q^\eps Z_1^{1/3}$. Since $t_1\sqrt{Z_1}=\sqrt{x/q}\,t_1^{1/2}$ and $t_1Z_1^{1/3}=(x/q)^{1/3}t_1^{2/3}$,
\[
\MT(x;q)=A_0\Delta_qI\sqrt{xq}\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{1/2}\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_2)+R,
\]
\[
|R|\le c_5(\eps)\,q^{1+\eps}\Bigl(\frac xq\Bigr)^{1/3}\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{2/3}\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_2),
\]
where we used $A_0\le1$. By~\eqref{eq:eta-bound}, $\sum_{t_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{2/3}\le\prod_p(1+2p^{-4/3})$ and $\sum_{t_2}\eta(t_2)\le\prod_p(1+2p^{-2})$, both absolute constants. So $|R|\le c_6(\eps)x^{1/3}q^{2/3+\eps}$.

\emph{The constant is $h(q)$.} The two finite sums are Euler products over the primes dividing $q$:
\[
\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{1/2}=\prod_{p\|q}\Bigl(1+\frac{\sqrt p}{p^2-2}\Bigr),\qquad\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_2)=\prod_{p^2\mid q}\Bigl(1+\frac1{p^2-2}\Bigr).
\]
Multiplying the absolutely convergent products $A_0$ and $\Delta_q$ factor by factor, the local factor at $p$ of the main coefficient is
\begin{align*}
p\nmid q:&\quad\Bigl(1-\tfrac2{p^2}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\tfrac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\tfrac p{p^2-2}\Bigr)=\frac{(p-1)(p^2+p-2)}{p^3}=\frac{(p-1)^2(p+2)}{p^3}=a_p,\\
p\,\|\,q:&\quad\Bigl(1-\tfrac2{p^2}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\tfrac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\tfrac{\sqrt p}{p^2-2}\Bigr)=\frac{(p-1)(p^2-2+\sqrt p)}{p^3}=b_p,\\
p^2\mid q:&\quad\Bigl(1-\tfrac2{p^2}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\tfrac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\tfrac1{p^2-2}\Bigr)=\frac{(p-1)(p^2-1)}{p^3}=c_p .
\end{align*}
Together with the factor $I$, this is exactly $h(q)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Since $b_p/a_p\ge1-1/p$ and $c_p/a_p=(p+1)/(p+2)\ge1-1/p$, we have $h(q)\ge IA_h\,\varphi(q)/q\gg_\eps q^{-\eps}$, where $A_h=\prod_pa_p>0$ (\cref{prop:poly}(0)). So \cref{prop:MT} gives, for $x\ge1$ and $1\le q\le x$,
\[
\MT(x;q)=h(q)\sqrt{xq}\,\bigl(1+O_\eps(x^{2\eps}(q/x)^{1/6})\bigr),
\]
because the relative error is $\ll_\eps q^{2\eps}(q/x)^{1/6}$ and $q^{2\eps}\le x^{2\eps}$ for $q\le x$. (Without the restriction $q\le x$ the display can fail. Since $0\le q\,m\,B(x/(qm))\le x$ and $\sum_t\eta(t)<\infty$ (\cref{lem:eta}), \eqref{eq:MT} gives $0\le\MT(x;q)\ll x$ for all $x>0$. Hence $\MT(x;1)/(h(1)\sqrt x)\to0$ as $x\to0$, whereas for $\eps>1/12$ the displayed error term $x^{2\eps}x^{-1/6}$ tends to $0$.) The relative error is not small when $q\asymp x$. This is why the asymptotic formula of \cref{thm:main}(iii) requires $Y\le x^{1-\delta}$, whereas the error term in~(ii), which keeps $\MT$ unexpanded, has no such restriction. The numerical data in \cref{sec:numerics} suggest that, after summation over the moduli, the secondary term has relative size roughly proportional to $\sqrt{Y/x}$. That is consistent with, but sharper than, the proved bound.
\end{remark}
\section{The variance for a single modulus}\label{sec:single}

\begin{proposition}[Single-modulus variance]\label{prop:single}
For every $\eps>0$ there is $c_7(\eps)$ such that for all real $x\ge2$ and all integers $1\le q\le x$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $|V(x;q)-\MT(x;q)|\le c_7(\eps)\bigl(x^{5/3+\eps}/q+\sqrt x\bigr)$;
\item $|V(x;q)-h(q)\sqrt{xq}|\le c_7(\eps)\bigl(x^{1/3}q^{2/3+\eps}+x^{5/3+\eps}/q+\sqrt x\bigr)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) By \cref{prop:identity}, which holds for all $x\ge1$ and $q\in\N$,
\[
V(x;q)-\MT(x;q)=2\sum_{1\le h\le x/q}D_x(hq)+\Bigl(Q(x)-\frac{6x}{\pi^2}\Bigr)-2x\sum_{l=1}^qg(q,l)E(x;q,l).
\]
For $1\le h\le x/q$ the integer $m=hq$ satisfies $1\le m\le x$. Since $x\ge2$, \cref{prop:pairs} applies to each of the at most $x/q$ terms. (This is the only place where $x\ge2$ rather than $x\ge1$ is needed.) It gives
\[
\Bigl|2\sum_{1\le h\le x/q}D_x(hq)\Bigr|\le2\cdot\frac xq\cdot c_3(\eps)x^{2/3+\eps}=2c_3(\eps)\frac{x^{5/3+\eps}}q .
\]
\Cref{prop:trivial}(i) gives $|Q(x)-6x/\pi^2|\le c_0\sqrt x$. \Cref{prop:trivial}(ii) gives
\[
\Bigl|2x\sum_lg(q,l)E(x;q,l)\Bigr|\le2c_0\frac{x^{3/2}}q\le2c_0\frac{x^{5/3+\eps}}q,
\]
since $x\ge1$. By the triangle inequality, (i) holds with $c_7(\eps)\ge2c_3(\eps)+2c_0$.

(ii) \Cref{prop:MT} gives $|\MT(x;q)-h(q)\sqrt{xq}|\le c_6(\eps)x^{1/3}q^{2/3+\eps}$. Combining this with (i) by the triangle inequality proves (ii) with
\[
c_7(\eps)=\max\bigl\{2c_3(\eps)+2c_0,\ c_6(\eps)\bigr\},
\]
and (i) remains true with this larger constant.
\end{proof}

\section{Provenance}\label{app:provenance}

The mathematics in \cref{sec:prelim,sec:densities,sec:identity,sec:pairs,sec:sawtooth,sec:single,sec:poly,sec:assembly} is an edited presentation of an archived run of a multi-agent proof pipeline in which language models proposed, proved and refereed the results. This appendix records where the material comes from. A proposition-by-proposition map, with every editorial change and correction, is in \texttt{manuscript/changes.md}.

\emph{Archive.}
\begin{itemize}
\item Source repository: \url{https://gitlab.com/mshepherd/squarefree-numbers}, archive label \texttt{zt-neutral}.
\item Archive commit: \texttt{ed0aebaf461b602601856bf1b693fd76893d9aba}.
\item Harness commit: \texttt{33aadc609359221ba5d81664438bce5f658f561c}.
\item Revision recorded for all run stages: \texttt{8dfc53d01e56c9949c42061fdbe907a98a12a5d7}.
\end{itemize}

\emph{Models and roles (as recorded).} The model identifiers are those recorded in the archive. The command-line tool versions are not model-weight versions, and model versions beyond these identifiers are unknown.
\begin{itemize}[before=\raggedright]
\item Planning and probing: \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol}; probing also \texttt{claude-sonnet-5-5}.
\item Numerics: \texttt{claude-sonnet-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol} produced candidate computations. The \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol} snapshot was accepted.
\item Proofs: \texttt{claude-sonnet-5-5} (prover).
\item Refereeing: \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol}. Each proposition was reviewed independently by both.
\item Integration (assembly audit): \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol}, independently.
\end{itemize}
Claude models ran under Claude Code 2.1.309 and Codex models under codex-cli 0.166.0.

\emph{Write-up stage.} This text was written by \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} (Claude Code 2.1.311) from the archived run. It was refereed by \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol} (the write-up stage records Claude Code 2.1.311 and codex-cli 0.166.0) in three rounds. Each round was followed by a revision, and the present version answers the third round. Some of the corrections described below were raised by these write-up referees.

\emph{Workflow.} The problem statement restricts $f$ to $\Z[t]$. It asks for the asymptotic behaviour of $V_f(x,y)$ in as large a range of $f(y)\le x$ as can be justified, and it accepts a weaker range or error term provided it is correct. The weight $f'(k)$ and the class~\eqref{eq:f-hyp} of polynomials used here are those of the problem statement; neither was changed. The numerical candidates were computed before any plan existed, and one was accepted on computational grounds only, not because of its fitted constants. Eight proof plans were written, and the plan \texttt{simplest@claude-opus-5-5} was selected by the project owner. It splits the argument into nine propositions P1--P9. In this text, P1 is \cref{prop:densities}, P2 is \cref{prop:identity}, P3 is \cref{prop:pairs}, P4 is \cref{prop:trivial}, P5 is \cref{prop:sawtooth}, P6 is \cref{prop:MT}, P7 is \cref{prop:single}, P8 is \cref{prop:poly}, and P9 is \cref{thm:main} with its proof in \cref{sec:assembly}. All nine proofs passed both referees in the first round, with only cosmetic remarks. Both integrators found that the propositions compose to the stated theorem without loss and without interface mismatches. The project owner's recorded decision reads: ``Let's just assume the proof is correct and complete.'' A separate read-only operator audit found no substantive gap and left final mathematical acceptance to the project owner. The corrections made in this text are local and fall into three groups, listed individually in \texttt{changes.md}: (a) those recorded in the operator audit (the normalisation and convergence wording in P1(iii), the endpoint $k=1$ in P8, and unused numerical remarks in P6 and P8); (b) cosmetic points raised by the run's referees; and (c) points raised at the write-up stage. Group~(c) contains one clarification of an archived auxiliary statement. For an infinite interval, the Euler--Maclaurin lemma in the archived P5 proof says that ``the same holds'' under the hypotheses $G,G'\to0$, $G''\in L^1$. Read as an identity between a convergent series and a convergent integral, this is false in that generality. \Cref{lem:EM} keeps exactly the archived hypotheses and states what letting $b\to\infty$ gives: the difference between the partial sums and the partial integrals converges, and the formula holds whenever the series or the integral converges. Both archived applications have absolutely convergent series and integrals, so no proposition and no step of the argument changes. No decision of the project owner on this point is recorded, and \texttt{changes.md} lists it for the owner's attention. The other items in group~(c) concern only the exposition of this text, for example an arithmetic slip in an earlier version of the write-up, and do not touch the archived arguments. Agreement between models is evidence, not certification; the arguments are reproduced here in full so that they can be checked directly.

\emph{Independent checks during the run.} Before acceptance, the operator compared both numerical candidates on overlapping rows and recomputed some rows by brute force. One integrator recomputed all $16$ rows for $k^2+1$ and $k^3+2$ at $x=250000$ by direct counting. The other computed $\sum f'(k)\MT(x;f(k))$ independently and compared it with the data. These checks are recorded in the archive. The computations in \cref{sec:numerics} were redone for this write-up as described there.

\emph{Literature.} The run used the papers supplied with the problem and literature up to 2010, with the single exception of Brüdern--Wooley~\cite{BruedernWooley2011}, which was supplied. The present text cites only works in the supplied corpus. See \texttt{README.md} for the limitations of the bibliography.

\section{Provenance}\label{app:provenance}

The mathematics in \cref{sec:prelim,sec:densities,sec:identity,sec:pairs,sec:sawtooth,sec:single,sec:poly,sec:assembly} is an edited presentation of an archived run of a multi-agent proof pipeline in which language models proposed, proved and refereed the results. This appendix records where the material comes from. A proposition-by-proposition map, with every editorial change and correction, is in \texttt{manuscript/changes.md}.

\emph{Archive.}
\begin{itemize}
\item Source repository: \url{https://gitlab.com/mshepherd/squarefree-numbers}, archive label \texttt{zt-neutral}.
\item Archive commit: \texttt{ed0aebaf461b602601856bf1b693fd76893d9aba}.
\item Harness commit: \texttt{33aadc609359221ba5d81664438bce5f658f561c}.
\item Revision recorded for all run stages: \texttt{8dfc53d01e56c9949c42061fdbe907a98a12a5d7}.
\end{itemize}

\emph{Models and roles (as recorded).} The model identifiers are those recorded in the archive. The command-line tool versions are not model-weight versions, and model versions beyond these identifiers are unknown.
\begin{itemize}[before=\raggedright]
\item Planning and probing: \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol}; probing also \texttt{claude-sonnet-5-5}.
\item Numerics: \texttt{claude-sonnet-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol} produced candidate computations. The \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol} snapshot was accepted.
\item Proofs: \texttt{claude-sonnet-5-5} (prover).
\item Refereeing: \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol}. Each proposition was reviewed independently by both.
\item Integration (assembly audit): \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol}, independently.
\end{itemize}
Claude models ran under Claude Code 2.1.309 and Codex models under codex-cli 0.166.0.

\emph{Write-up stage.} This text was written by \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} (Claude Code 2.1.311) from the archived run. It was refereed by \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol} (the write-up stage records Claude Code 2.1.311 and codex-cli 0.166.0) in three rounds. Each round was followed by a revision, and the present version answers the third round. Some of the corrections described below were raised by these write-up referees.

\emph{Workflow.} The problem statement restricts $f$ to $\Z[t]$. It asks for the asymptotic behaviour of $V_f(x,y)$ in as large a range of $f(y)\le x$ as can be justified, and it accepts a weaker range or error term provided it is correct. The weight $f'(k)$ and the class~\eqref{eq:f-hyp} of polynomials used here are those of the problem statement; neither was changed. The numerical candidates were computed before any plan existed, and one was accepted on computational grounds only, not because of its fitted constants. Eight proof plans were written, and the plan \texttt{simplest@claude-opus-5-5} was selected by the project owner. It splits the argument into nine propositions P1--P9. In this text, P1 is \cref{prop:densities}, P2 is \cref{prop:identity}, P3 is \cref{prop:pairs}, P4 is \cref{prop:trivial}, P5 is \cref{prop:sawtooth}, P6 is \cref{prop:MT}, P7 is \cref{prop:single}, P8 is \cref{prop:poly}, and P9 is \cref{thm:main} with its proof in \cref{sec:assembly}. All nine proofs passed both referees in the first round, with only cosmetic remarks. Both integrators found that the propositions compose to the stated theorem without loss and without interface mismatches. The project owner's recorded decision reads: ``Let's just assume the proof is correct and complete.'' A separate read-only operator audit found no substantive gap and left final mathematical acceptance to the project owner. The corrections made in this text are local and fall into three groups, listed individually in \texttt{changes.md}: (a) those recorded in the operator audit (the normalisation and convergence wording in P1(iii), the endpoint $k=1$ in P8, and unused numerical remarks in P6 and P8); (b) cosmetic points raised by the run's referees; and (c) points raised at the write-up stage. Group~(c) contains one clarification of an archived auxiliary statement. For an infinite interval, the Euler--Maclaurin lemma in the archived P5 proof says that ``the same holds'' under the hypotheses $G,G'\to0$, $G''\in L^1$. Read as an identity between a convergent series and a convergent integral, this is false in that generality. \Cref{lem:EM} keeps exactly the archived hypotheses and states what letting $b\to\infty$ gives: the difference between the partial sums and the partial integrals converges, and the formula holds whenever the series or the integral converges. Both archived applications have absolutely convergent series and integrals, so no proposition and no step of the argument changes. No decision of the project owner on this point is recorded, and \texttt{changes.md} lists it for the owner's attention. The other items in group~(c) concern only the exposition of this text, for example an arithmetic slip in an earlier version of the write-up, and do not touch the archived arguments. Agreement between models is evidence, not certification; the arguments are reproduced here in full so that they can be checked directly.

\emph{Independent checks during the run.} Before acceptance, the operator compared both numerical candidates on overlapping rows and recomputed some rows by brute force. One integrator recomputed all $16$ rows for $k^2+1$ and $k^3+2$ at $x=250000$ by direct counting. The other computed $\sum f'(k)\MT(x;f(k))$ independently and compared it with the data. These checks are recorded in the archive. The computations in \cref{sec:numerics} were redone for this write-up as described there.

\emph{Literature.} The run used the papers supplied with the problem and literature up to 2010, with the single exception of Brüdern--Wooley~\cite{BruedernWooley2011}, which was supplied. The present text cites only works in the supplied corpus. See \texttt{README.md} for the limitations of the bibliography.

    proof line 11): "If b = ∞ and F, F' → 0, F'' ∈ L^1, the same holds with the
    terms at b dropped." *Problem:* read as an identity between a convergent
    series `Σ_{n>a} F(n)` and a convergent integral `∫_a^∞ F`, this is false in
    that generality: `G(u) = cos(log u)/u` on `[1, ∞)` has `G, G' → 0` and
    `G'' = O(u^{-3}) ∈ L^1`, but `∫_1^X G = sin(log X)` has no limit as X → ∞
    (raised by the write-up referee `codex:gpt-6.1-sol` in round 1; confirmed
    by both round-3 referees, `feedback/0.json` and `feedback/1.json`).
    *History in this write-up:* rounds 2–3 added the hypothesis "`∫_a^∞ G`
    converges" to Lemma 2.6 and flagged it for Markus's acknowledgement. The
    round-3 referee `codex:gpt-6.1-sol` asked for Markus's decision before
    that change could be treated as accepted (`feedback/1.json`, issue 1). The
    supplied material records no such decision: there is no `brief.md`, and
    `source/interventions.md` has no entry on it. *Present version (round 4):*
    the added hypothesis has been removed. Lemma 2.6 now has exactly the
    archived hypotheses (`G ∈ C²[a, ∞)`, `G, G' → 0`, `G'' ∈ L^1`). Its
    conclusion is the statement that letting b → ∞ in the finite formula
    actually gives: `lim_{b→∞}(Σ_{a<n≤b} G(n) − ∫_a^b G)` exists and equals
    `ψ(a)G(a) − ψ_2(a)G'(a) − ∫_a^∞ ψ_2 G''`. In particular, the series
    converges if and only if the integral does, and then the formula holds with
    b = ∞. This is one reading of "the same holds", and under it the archived
    clause is true as stated. The cos(log u)/u example is kept in the proof to
    show why the precise form is needed. The lemma also says explicitly that G
    may be complex-valued, as in the archived application to `u^{-s}`; the
    proof applies to the real and imaginary parts. *Applications:* both
    archived applications have absolutely convergent series and integrals:
    `G(u) = u^{-s}`, `Re s > 1`, in Proposition 6.1(a) (P5 line 23–24, where
    the archive itself evaluates `∫_N^∞ u^{-s} = N^{1-s}/(s−1)`), and
    `Φ(u) = Z/u² − Z²/u⁴` on `(T, ∞)` in Proposition 6.1(b) (P5 line 62: "all
    integrals converge absolutely"). Section 6 now says this at both places.
    No proposition, no step of the P5 argument and no constant changes, so this
    is not a source gap and no `SOURCE_GAP.md` is written. Because it is still
    a write-up-stage choice of how to state an archived lemma, it is listed for
    Markus's attention in §10.
20. [c] **Proposition 6.1(b), arithmetic of the final sum** (write-up referee
    `codex:gpt-6.1-sol`, round 1; objection, stated inline: the sum of the
    bounds for `R_1, …, R_5` is `449Λ/8`, not `< 56.1Λ`). The round-1 manuscript wrote the
    sum of the bounds for `R_1, …, R_5` as `< 56.1Λ`. It equals
    `449/8 Λ = 56.125Λ`. This was an error introduced in the write-up: the
    archived P5 proof (line 65) has the correct bound `< 57Λ`, with the
    decimal approximation "56.1" written as a rounding. Corrected to
    `= 449/8 Λ < 57Λ`. The constant `c_1 = 60` is unchanged.
21. [c] **Remark 6.3, range of the relative-error formula** (write-up referee
    `codex:gpt-6.1-sol`, round 2; that review file is not in this workspace). The remark (write-up
    material, §5) replaced `q^{2ε}` by `x^{2ε}` without stating `q ≤ x`, while
    Proposition 6.2 just above it holds for all `x > 0`. The formula is now
    stated for `x ≥ 1`, `1 ≤ q ≤ x`, with the reason (`q^{2ε} ≤ x^{2ε}`).
    The remark also notes why the restriction is needed: `0 ≤ MT(x;q) ≪ x` by
    (1.7) and Lemma 2.4, so `MT(x;1)/(h(1)√x) → 0` as `x → 0`, while the error
    term tends to 0 for `ε > 1/12`. Proposition 6.2 and the main theorem are
    untouched.

## 4a. Statements stated more explicitly or more strongly than the archived statement files

Each item is either proved in the archived proof (with line reference) or
proved in full in the manuscript. None is used to strengthen the main theorem.
(Identified as unrecorded by the round-1 write-up referee `claude-opus-5-5`,
whose objection was that the manuscript stated some auxiliary results more
strongly than the archived statement files without saying so.)

* **Proposition 6.2 (P6), range.** `source/props/P6/statement.md` states the
  bound for real `x ≥ 1` and integers `1 ≤ q ≤ x`. The manuscript states it
  for all real `x > 0` and all `q ∈ ℕ`, adding "in particular for `x ≥ 1`,
  `1 ≤ q ≤ x`". Source: P6 proof Step 2, line 50 ("No use was made of q ≤ x or
  x ≥ 1 in this step; the error bound holds for all x > 0, q ≥ 1"), and the
  Conclusion, line 71.
* **Proposition 6.1(b) (P5(b)), explicit constant.** The statement file has
  "an absolute constant c_1"; the manuscript states `c_1 = 60`. Source: P5
  proof line 37 ("I show this with c_1 = 60").
* **Proposition 3.3 (P4), explicit constant.** The statement file has "an
  absolute constant c_0"; the manuscript states `c_0 = 3e^{2ζ(3/2)}`. Source: P4
  proof line 68. The manuscript also notes, as in P4 proof line 17, that `q ≤ x`
  is not used in (ii).
* **Lemma 3.2 (P4 Step 3).** `|T_r(y) − ν_r y| ≤ 3·2^{ω(r)} √y` for all `y > 0` is
  P4 proof estimate (3), lines 45–48. Its case `r = 1`, `|Q(y) − 6y/π²| ≤ 3√y`
  for all `y > 0`, extends P4(i) (stated for `x ≥ 1`, line 13) to `0 < y < 1`.
  That case is trivial: `Q(y) = 0` and `6y/π² < 3√y`. It is not used.
* **Lemma 2.2, strict inequality.** P1 proof line 14 and P3 proof line 33 use
  `N/L + θ` with `|θ| ≤ 1`. Lemma 2.2 states and proves `|θ| < 1`. Every use
  needs only `|θ| ≤ 1`.
* **Proposition 5.1 (P3), constant.** `(3 + 9C(ε))` instead of
  `2(1+τ*) + 1 + 14τ*`; see §4 item 3.

## 5. Material added after the run

None of the following is used in a proof.

* **Section 1 background**: Vaughan's theorem for the full variance (2005,
  (1.12)–(1.16)), the earlier `x²𝓕(x/Y)` results it quotes, and the
  Brüdern–Wooley theorem (2011, Theorem in §1), all read from the supplied PDFs.

  elementary argument of Evelyn and Linfoot giving
  `r_k(n) = S_k(n) n + O(n^{2/(k+1)+ε})` for sums of two k-free numbers (read

# Changes: from the archived run to the manuscript

This file maps every result in `main.tex` to its source in the archived run
(`source/`), records the two referee reports for each proposition, and lists
every notation change, merged argument, correction and addition.

Archive: `source/` (archive label `zt-neutral`, archive commit
`ed0aebaf461b602601856bf1b693fd76893d9aba`); selected plan
`simplest@claude-opus-5-5` (`source/plan.md`, `source/plan.json`).
For every proposition PN, `source/props/PN/review-v1-0.json` is the review by
`claude-opus-5-5` and `source/props/PN/review-v1-1.json` the review by
`codex:gpt-6.1-sol`. Both reviewers passed all nine propositions in round 1
(severities: none or cosmetic). The assembly/integration reports are
`source/report/assembly-claude-opus-5-5.md`,
`source/report/assembly-codex-gpt-6.1-sol.md`,
`source/report/integration-*.json` and `source/report/integration.json`.

The theorem is stated with exactly the strength, ranges, hypotheses and
error terms of the plan's main theorem and of P9. The weight `f'(k)` and the
class of `f` are unchanged. No proposition is used outside its stated range.
No mathematical change was made beyond the local corrections listed in §4.
Each is tagged in §4 by its origin:

* **(a)** recorded in the operator audit (`source/interventions.md`,
  2026-11-03 10:21, and Markus's 2026-11-03 "result" entry: P1(iii)
  normalisation/convergence wording, P8 endpoint explanation, unused P6/P8
  numerical notes);
* **(b)** raised by the run's own referees (`source/props/PN/review-v1-*.json`),
  all cosmetic;
* **(c)** raised at the write-up stage, by the writer or by the write-up
  referees (`claude-opus-5-5`, `codex:gpt-6.1-sol`). These are not covered by
  the recorded audit.

None of them weakens a statement or changes the main theorem. A few auxiliary
statements are stated slightly more strongly or more explicitly than in the
archived statement files; each such case is taken from the archived proof or
proved in full in the manuscript, and is listed in §4a. One archived
auxiliary statement, the infinite-interval clause of the Euler–Maclaurin
lemma in the P5 proof (Lemma 2.6), is stated more precisely: its hypotheses
are kept exactly, and its conclusion is stated in the form that is true under
them (§4, item 19). No decision by Markus on this point is recorded in the
supplied material; it is listed for his attention in §10.

**Feedback files.** The write-up was refereed in three rounds by
`claude-opus-5-5` and `codex:gpt-6.1-sol`. Only the round-3 review files are
in this workspace: `feedback/0.json` (`claude-opus-5-5`, verdict pass) and
`feedback/1.json` (`codex:gpt-6.1-sol`, verdict revise), both reviewing the
previous version (manuscript hash `79e72fca…`). They are answered in §9. The
round-1 and round-2 review files are historical and are **not** in this
package. §7 and §8, and every mention of a round-1 or round-2 objection
elsewhere in this file, are the writer's own summaries, written when those
reviews were answered. They cannot be checked against the original files
here. Wherever the content of such an objection matters, it is stated inline.

## 1. Map of results

| Manuscript | Archived statement / proof | Reviews |
|---|---|---|
| Theorem 1.1 (i), (ii), (iii) | `plan.md` "Main theorem"; `props/P9/statement.md`, `props/P9/proof.md`; composition audited in both assembly reports | P9: `review-v1-0.json` (Opus, pass, none), `review-v1-1.json` (Sol, pass, none) |
| Theorem 1.1, positivity of C_f | `props/P8/statement.md` claim (0) | see P8 |
| Remark 1.2 (range) | `plan.md` "Range" paragraph; assembly reports §5 (Opus) and §4 (Sol) | — |
| Remark 1.3 (C_t = Vaughan's c_2) | `plan.md` consistency check 1; Opus assembly report §3 | — (numerical in the run; see §5 below) |
| Lemma 2.1 (tail bound) | P3 proof Step 0 `(*)`; also P1 proof (i), P4 proof (0), P5 proof (c) | P1, P3, P4, P5 |
| Lemma 2.2 (residue-class count) | P1 proof (i) (`source/props/P1/proof.md` line 14); P3 proof Step 2 (line 33) | P1, P3 |
| Lemma 2.3 (divisor bounds) | standard facts used in P3, P5(c), P8 §3.2–3.3; MV (2.20) as cited by the Sol referee of P3 | P3, P5, P8 |
| Euler products (2.1) | used throughout P1, P3, P5, P8; cited as MV Theorem 1.9 | — |
| Lemma 2.4 (η, κ, A_0) | P1(v) and its proof; P2 notation (absolute convergence of MT); P6 proof Step 0 | P1, P2, P6 |
| Lemma 2.5 (coprime pairs) | P1 proof (iv) (the product I(t)) and P3 proof Step 4 | P1, P3 |
| Lemma 2.6 (Euler–Maclaurin) | P5 proof §0, Lemma EM (`source/props/P5/proof.md` lines 9–11); conclusion of the b = ∞ clause stated precisely, archived hypotheses unchanged, see §4 item 19 | P5 |
| Proposition 3.1 | P1 (i)–(v) | P1: Opus pass/none; Sol pass/cosmetic |
| Lemma 3.2 | P4 proof (ii) Step 3, estimate (3) for all y > 0 (`source/props/P4/proof.md` lines 33–48); P4 proof (i) (line 13) is its case r = 1 | P4 |
| Proposition 3.3 | P4 (i), (ii); explicit c_0 from P4 proof "Conclusion" (line 68) | P4: Opus pass/none; Sol pass/none |
| Proposition 4.1 | P2 | P2: Opus pass/none; Sol pass/none |
| Proposition 5.1 | P3 | P3: Opus pass/cosmetic; Sol pass/none |

| Proposition 6.2 | P6; range x > 0, q ≥ 1 from P6 proof Step 2 (line 50) and "Conclusion" (line 71) | P6: Opus pass/none; Sol pass/cosmetic |
| Proposition 7.1 | P7 | P7: Opus pass/none; Sol pass/none |
| Proposition 8.1 (0), (a)–(c) | P8 | P8: Opus pass/cosmetic; Sol pass/cosmetic |
| Lemma 8.2 (local factors) | P8 proof §0 "Elementary identities" | P8 |
| Lemma 8.3 (root counts) | P8 proof §0 "The function ρ" | P8 |
| Lemma 8.4 (shape of F) | P8 proof §0 "Shape of F" | P8 |
| Lemma 8.5 (monotone weights) | P8 proof §3.4 "Lemma" | P8 |
| Section 9 | P9 proof §0–§3 | P9 |
| Section 10 | `source/numerics/` (accepted snapshot `snapshot-nu6pbkr4`, candidate `codex-gpt-6.1-sol`), assembly reports §3–§4 (Opus) and §6 (Sol); recomputed by `manuscript/reproduce.py` | — |
| Appendix B | `provenance.json`, `source/interventions.md` | — |

## 2. Notation changes

| Archived | Manuscript | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `tau_p` (local factor of C_f; plan, P8, P9, reports) | `σ_p` | `τ(n)` is the divisor function (P3, P8) |
| `c_0 = -4ζ(-1/2)` (P8 proof) | `I` (as in P5) | one name for one constant; `c_0` is now the absolute constant `3e^{2ζ(3/2)}` of P4 |
| `A_p, B_p, D_p` (P8 proof) | `a_p, b_p, c_p` (as in the Sol assembly report) | `B` is the sawtooth function |
| `A = ∏ A_p`, `b(q)`, `u = b*μ` (P8 proof) | `A_h`, `h^♮(q)`, `w = μ*h^♮` | avoid clashes with `A(m)`, `b_p` and P5's `b` |
| `c_1, c_2, c_3, c_5` (P8 shape constants), `C_1 = ∏_{p∈P_0} p^2`, truncation parameter `E` | `γ_1, …, γ_4`, `C_P`, `W` | avoid clashes with `c_1 = 60` (P5), `C_1` (Vaughan) and `E(x;q,l)` |
| `δ_q` (P5) | `Δ_q` | `δ` is the range parameter of the theorem |
| `f(t) = κ(t)1[(t,q)=1]`, `b = μ*f` (P5(c) proof) | `κ_q(t)`, `β = μ*κ_q` (the plan's name) | `f` is the polynomial |
| `A(u)`, `E_1, …, E_5` (P5(b) proof) | `Φ(u)`, `R_1, …, R_5` | `A(m)`, `E(x;q,l)` |
| `t = t_1 t_2 t_3`, `Z(t_2)` (P6 proof) | `t = t_0 t_1 t_2` (subscript = min(v_p(q), 2)), `Z_1` | mnemonic indexing |
| local `h(p)` (P1 proof (iii)) | `u(p)` | `h(q)` is the main-term function |
| `κ_r` (P4 proof) | `ν_r` | `κ(t)` |
| `E_1, E_2, E_3` (P3 proof) | `𝓔_1, 𝓔_2, 𝓔_3` | `E(x;q,l)` |
| generic `c(ε)` in P3, P5, P6, P7, P8 | `c_3(ε)`, `c_5(ε)`, `c_6(ε)`, `c_7(ε)`, `c_8(f), c_8(f,ε)` | to compose constants explicitly in §7 and §9 |
| Vaughan's modulus bound `Q` in `V(x,Q)` (Vaughan 2005, quoted in §1.2) | `Y`, so `V(x,Y)` | `Q(x)` and `Q(x;q,l)` are the counting functions (write-up referee, round 1) |
| actual ratio `ratio_actual` (snapshot) | `ϱ = f(y)/x` (§10.5) | distinguish from the target ratio `r` |

## 3. Merged arguments

* **Tail bound** `Σ_{a>w} a^{-2} ≤ 2/w`: proved four times in the archive (P1 (i),
  P3 `(*)`, P4 (0), P5 (c)); stated once as Lemma 2.1 (P3's version, valid for all w > 0).
* **Counting integers in a residue class** (`N/L + θ`): P1 (i) and P3 Step 2 →
  Lemma 2.2.
* **Coprime pairs of squarefree numbers**: the Euler product
  `Σ μ(a)μ(b)/(ab)^2 = ∏_{p∤e}(1-2/p^2)` was derived twice by "local choices"
  (P1 proof (iv), P3 proof Step 4). Lemma 2.5 states it once. Its proof groups
  the pairs by n = ab, which turns the sum into the multiplicative series
  `Σ μ(n)2^{ω(n)} n^{-2} 1[(n,e)=1]`. This is the same computation in a
  shorter form.
* **Squarefree numbers coprime to r**: P4 (i) (count of Q(x)) and P4 (ii) Step 3
  (count of T_r) are the same estimate; Lemma 3.2 proves the general case, and
  Proposition 3.3(i) is its case r = 1. The constant `3√x` of P4 (i) is unchanged.
* **Facts on η, κ, A_0** scattered over P1, P2, P6 → Lemma 2.4.

## 4. Corrections (all local; no weakening of any statement)

1. [a] **P1(iii), normalisation** (Sol review of P1, "other issues"; operator audit).
   The proof states `q·μ(d) g_d/d²·1[g_d | n] = ∏_{p|d} h(p)`, with an
   extraneous factor q. Corrected in Proposition 3.1(iii): `μ(d) g_d/d² 1[g_d|n]
   = ∏_{p|d} u(p)` and `q g(q,n) = Σ_d μ²(d) ∏_{p|d} u(p)`.
2. [a] **P1(iii), convergence** (Sol review of P1, main objection, cosmetic;
   operator audit). The claim `Σ_p |h(p)| ≤ Σ_p p^{-2}` is false for p | q
   (e.g. q = n = 2). Corrected: `|u(p)| = p^{-2}` for p ∤ q, and `|u(p)| ≤ 1` for
   the finitely many p | q, so the series converges absolutely.
3. [b] **P3 Step 3, constant** (Opus review of P3). The proof writes
   `2·(π²/6)·Σ e^{-2}(2e/z) ≤ (4π²/(3z)) Σ 1/e`; the left side equals
   `(2π²/(3z)) Σ 1/e`. The original inequality was true but overestimated by a factor 2. The manuscript uses
   the correct value and the bound `7τ(m)/z` instead of `14τ(m)/z`. The final
   constant `(3 + 9C(ε))` replaces `2(1+τ*) + 1 + 14τ*`. Statement unchanged.
4. [a] **P8 §3.4, endpoint k = 1** (Opus review of P8, cosmetic; operator audit;
   flagged as "P8 endpoint clarification" in `interventions.md`). The proof
   treats the closed first interval `[1, β]` as `(1-δ, β]`. That needs F to be defined and
   monotone left of 1, which fails e.g. for f = 3t − 1. Corrected by stating
   the counting lemma (Lemma 8.5) for arbitrary intervals (open, closed or
   half-open). Its proof only uses that `k_1 − e` and `k_n + e` lie outside the
   interval. The closed interval `[1, β]` is then covered directly, and the constant
   `3(2d−1) ≤ 6d` in eq. (8.10) (source eq. (3.9)) is unchanged.
5. [b] **P8 §3.5, implicit error term** (Opus review of P8). The source writes
   `O(Y^{3/2} y^{-1/2})` for the term `(2/3)(Y^{3/2} − f(1)^{3/2})·O(y^{-1/2})`
   without saying where it comes from. The assembly display in §8.3 now shows
   it. The short-sum bound keeps the factor `(1 + log W)` (P8 (3.6)) explicitly,
   and it is absorbed by the choice `ε ≤ 1/8` (the source absorbs it into
   `E^{2ε}`). The final bound is unchanged.
6. [b] **P8 §3.2(ii), constant dependence** (Opus review of P8). The bound
   `(2d)^{ω(n)} ≤ C n^ε` has a constant depending on d; this is now stated
   (`C(f, ε)`).
7. [b] **P2, wording** (Opus review of P2). The parenthetical after (3) ("finitely
   many nonzero terms after the bracket is rewritten") is replaced by: the
   bracket vanishes for `q m_t(q) > x` (twice an empty sum), and each of the
   three series obtained by splitting it converges absolutely.
8. [b] **P4 (i), wording** (Opus review of P4). "Every squarefree-indicator
   identity gives" → derived from `μ²(n) = Σ_{d²|n} μ(d)` (Lemma 3.2).
9. [b] **P5(b), small s** (Opus review of P5). The two quantities both lie in
   `[0, Λ/4]`, so their difference is at most `Λ/4` (source: `Λ/2`). The constant
   `c_1 = 60` is kept.
10. [b] **P9, real-variable hypothesis** (Opus review of P9). The step
    `f(k) ≤ f(y)` for real y uses `f'(t) ≥ 1` for all real `t ≥ 1`. This is
    now explicit in (1.1) and in §9. The convention `1 ≤ k ≤ y` (integers) is
    explicit in (1.2). The constants `c(ε/3)`, `c(f, ε/3)` and their
    combination are written out in §9.
11. [b] **P9 remark on δ < 1/9** (Opus review of P9). Non-emptiness of the range
    holds for x > 1; stated so.
12. [b] **P7, role of x ≥ 2** (Opus review of P7). Noted in the proof of
    Proposition 7.1 that x ≥ 2 is needed only for P3.
13. [b] **P3, n ≥ 1** (Opus review of P3). C_x(m) counts positive n; explicit in
    eq. (4.1).
14. [b] **P1(iii), sign of n** (Opus review of P1). Stated for squarefree `n ∈ ℕ`,
    the only case used.
15. [b] **P5, citation "MV Thm B.5"** (Opus review of P5: not found in the
    supplied PDF). Appendix B of Montgomery–Vaughan is not in the supplied
    corpus. Its §1.3 refers to "Theorem B.5" for Euler–Maclaurin summation.
    The manuscript proves Lemma 2.6 directly and cites only MV §1.3 and
    Theorem 1.12 for comparison.
16. [a/b] **Unused numerical notes in the proofs** (not reproduced):
    * P2: the proof's check agreed only to ~1e-3 because of truncation (Opus
      review); replaced by the exact self-test in `reproduce.py`
      (`identity_selftest`, agreement 4.8e-10).
    * P6: the tail estimate `A_0 x/(q·3000)` wrongly contains 1/q (Sol review),
      and the difference 92 at (10^6, 1) is a truncation artefact (Opus review).
    * P8: "ρ(p²) ≈ ρ(p)/p, exact for these squarefree f" is false for root
      counts (should be ρ(p²) = ρ(p) for unramified p); Sol review and Sol
      assembly report §5. Also flagged in the operator audit.
    * P1, P5: numerical sanity checks are not reproduced; P5's constants were
      checked by the referees.

    (The P6 and P8 notes are group (a); the P2 note is group (b).)
17. [c] **Remark 1.2 (range of part (ii))**. The plan says statement (a)/(ii)
    "remains meaningful up to f(y) ~ x". The manuscript states only what is
    proved: the error term of (ii) is of smaller order than `x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}`
    for `x^{7/9+δ} ≤ Y ≤ x`. No lower bound for `Σ f'(k) MT(x; f(k))` is
    claimed.
18. [c] **References.** P8's "Hooley 1964 (background on rho only; not needed)" is
    dropped because no statement from it is used. The plan named a 1949 paper
    of Mirsky on pairs of squarefree numbers from memory. Earlier versions of
    this write-up cited Mirsky, Bull. AMS 55 (1949), from
    `bibliography-candidates.json`, without having consulted it. The round-1
    write-up referee `claude-opus-5-5` objected that this citation could not be
    checked against the supplied material, so the unverifiable historical
    attribution is dropped. Section 5 now quotes only what the
    supplied BGPVW (1998, §1) says about the related additive problem (see §5).
19. [c] **Lemma 2.6 / P5 Lemma EM, the case b = ∞.** *Archived text* (P5
    proof line 11): "If b = ∞ and F, F' → 0, F'' ∈ L^1, the same holds with the
    terms at b dropped." *Problem:* read as an identity between a convergent
    series `Σ_{n>a} F(n)` and a convergent integral `∫_a^∞ F`, this is false in
    that generality: `G(u) = cos(log u)/u` on `[1, ∞)` has `G, G' → 0` and
    `G'' = O(u^{-3}) ∈ L^1`, but `∫_1^X G = sin(log X)` has no limit as X → ∞
    (raised by the write-up referee `codex:gpt-6.1-sol` in round 1; confirmed
    by both round-3 referees, `feedback/0.json` and `feedback/1.json`).
    *History in this write-up:* rounds 2–3 added the hypothesis "`∫_a^∞ G`
    converges" to Lemma 2.6 and flagged it for Markus's acknowledgement. The
    round-3 referee `codex:gpt-6.1-sol` asked for Markus's decision before
    that change could be treated as accepted (`feedback/1.json`, issue 1). The
    supplied material records no such decision: there is no `brief.md`, and
    `source/interventions.md` has no entry on it. *Present version (round 4):*
    the added hypothesis has been removed. Lemma 2.6 now has exactly the
    archived hypotheses (`G ∈ C²[a, ∞)`, `G, G' → 0`, `G'' ∈ L^1`). Its
    conclusion is the statement that letting b → ∞ in the finite formula
    actually gives: `lim_{b→∞}(Σ_{a<n≤b} G(n) − ∫_a^b G)` exists and equals
    `ψ(a)G(a) − ψ_2(a)G'(a) − ∫_a^∞ ψ_2 G''`. In particular, the series
    converges if and only if the integral does, and then the formula holds with
    b = ∞. This is one reading of "the same holds", and under it the archived
    clause is true as stated. The cos(log u)/u example is kept in the proof to
    show why the precise form is needed. The lemma also says explicitly that G
    may be complex-valued, as in the archived application to `u^{-s}`; the
    proof applies to the real and imaginary parts. *Applications:* both
    archived applications have absolutely convergent series and integrals:
    `G(u) = u^{-s}`, `Re s > 1`, in Proposition 6.1(a) (P5 line 23–24, where
    the archive itself evaluates `∫_N^∞ u^{-s} = N^{1-s}/(s−1)`), and
    `Φ(u) = Z/u² − Z²/u⁴` on `(T, ∞)` in Proposition 6.1(b) (P5 line 62: "all
    integrals converge absolutely"). Section 6 now says this at both places.
    No proposition, no step of the P5 argument and no constant changes, so this
    is not a source gap and no `SOURCE_GAP.md` is written. Because it is still
    a write-up-stage choice of how to state an archived lemma, it is listed for
    Markus's attention in §10.
20. [c] **Proposition 6.1(b), arithmetic of the final sum** (write-up referee
    `codex:gpt-6.1-sol`, round 1; objection, stated inline: the sum of the
    bounds for `R_1, …, R_5` is `449Λ/8`, not `< 56.1Λ`). The round-1 manuscript wrote the
    sum of the bounds for `R_1, …, R_5` as `< 56.1Λ`. It equals
    `449/8 Λ = 56.125Λ`. This was an error introduced in the write-up: the
    archived P5 proof (line 65) has the correct bound `< 57Λ`, with the
    decimal approximation "56.1" written as a rounding. Corrected to
    `= 449/8 Λ < 57Λ`. The constant `c_1 = 60` is unchanged.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Regenerate every number in the manuscript's numerical tables and plots.
3	
4	Invoke from the workspace root:
5	
6	    python3 manuscript/reproduce.py
7	
8	What it does (details in manuscript/README.md):
9	
10	1. Copies the accepted snapshot's ``compute.py`` and ``counts.cpp`` from
11	   ``source/numerics/snapshot`` into a scratch work directory (after checking
12	   their SHA-256 against ``source/numerics/accepted.json``) and runs
13	   ``compute.py`` there unchanged.  That script compiles ``counts.cpp`` with
14	   clang++, re-runs its validations, recomputes V_f(x, y) on the full grid
15	   x = 2.5e5, ..., 2.56e8, and redoes the empirical fits.  The archived
16	   executable is not used.
17	2. Compares the regenerated ``results.json`` with the archived one.
18	3. Computes, with code in this file, the quantities of the theorem that are
19	   not part of the snapshot: the constant C_f (Euler product over p <= 1e7,
20	   with a rigorous bound for the omitted primes), Vaughan's constant c_2,
21	   the sums  sum_k f'(k) MT(x; f(k))  and  sum_k F(k) h(f(k))  at selected rows,
22	   and a self-test of the exact identity of Proposition 4.1 (P2).
23	4. Writes LaTeX table fragments and PGFPlots data files to
24	   ``manuscript/generated/`` and the index ``manuscript/reproduction.json``.
25	
26	No value is copied from proof prose or from the archived results; the
27	archived ``results.json`` is read only for the agreement check in step 2.
28	"""
29	import argparse
30	import hashlib
31	import itertools
32	import json
33	import math
34	import pathlib
35	import shutil
36	import subprocess
37	import sys
38	import time
39	from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_CEILING, ROUND_FLOOR
40	
41	import numpy as np
42	import mpmath as mp
43	import sympy
44	
45	HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
46	WS = HERE.parent
47	SNAP = WS / 'source' / 'numerics' / 'snapshot'
48	ACCEPTED = WS / 'source' / 'numerics' / 'accepted.json'
49	GEN = HERE / 'generated'
50	DEFAULT_WORK = WS / 'scratch' / 'reproduce-work'
51	MARKER = '.reproduce-work'
52	
53	NAMES = ['k^2+1', 'k^3+2', '2k+1']
54	TEXNAME = {'k^2+1': '$k^2+1$', 'k^3+2': '$k^3+2$', '2k+1': '$2k+1$', 't': '$t$ (formal)'}
55	POLY = {'k^2+1': (lambda k: k * k + 1, lambda k: 2 * k, 2),
56	        'k^3+2': (lambda k: k ** 3 + 2, lambda k: 3 * k * k, 3),
57	        '2k+1': (lambda k: 2 * k + 1, lambda k: 2, 1),
58	        't': (lambda k: k, lambda k: 1, 1)}
59	RATIOS = [.01, .02, .05, .1, .2, .4, .7, 1.]
60	PRIME_CUTOFFS = [10 ** 3, 10 ** 4, 10 ** 5, 10 ** 6, 10 ** 7]
61	# Rows of the exact-shape comparison (Table 5).  The linear polynomial has
62	# about x/2 moduli, so it is restricted to the two smallest sizes.
63	SHAPE_XS = {'k^2+1': [1000000, 16000000, 256000000],
64	            'k^3+2': [1000000, 16000000, 256000000],
65	            '2k+1': [250000, 1000000]}
66	
67	mp.mp.dps = 80
68	I_CONST = -4 * mp.zeta(mp.mpf(-1) / 2)          # I = -4 zeta(-1/2)
69	SIX_PI2 = 6 / mp.pi ** 2
70	
71	
72	def sha256(path):
73	    return hashlib.sha256(pathlib.Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
74	
75	
76	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
77	# 1. Snapshot re-run
78	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
79	
80	def run_snapshot(work, reuse):
81	    accepted = json.loads(ACCEPTED.read_text())['artifacts']
82	    for name in ['compute.py', 'counts.cpp']:
83	        if sha256(SNAP / name) != accepted[name]:
84	            raise RuntimeError(f'{name} does not match the accepted snapshot hash')
85	    elapsed = None
86	    if not (reuse and (work / 'results.json').exists()):
87	        if work.exists():
88	            # Only ever delete a directory that this script created itself.
89	            if any(work.iterdir()) and not (work / MARKER).exists():
90	                raise RuntimeError(f'{work} is not empty and was not created by reproduce.py; '
91	                                   'choose another --work directory')
92	            shutil.rmtree(work)
93	        work.mkdir(parents=True)
94	        (work / MARKER).write_text('scratch directory of manuscript/reproduce.py; safe to delete\n')
95	        for name in ['compute.py', 'counts.cpp']:
96	            shutil.copy2(SNAP / name, work / name)
97	        t0 = time.monotonic()
98	        subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(work / 'compute.py')], cwd=work, check=True)
99	        elapsed = time.monotonic() - t0
100	    for name in ['compute.py', 'counts.cpp']:
101	        if sha256(work / name) != accepted[name]:
102	            raise RuntimeError(f'work copy of {name} differs from the snapshot')
103	    results = json.loads((work / 'results.json').read_text())
104	    return results, elapsed
105	
106	
107	def all_rows(res, name):
108	    p = res['polynomials'][name]
109	    return p['rows'] + p['diagnostic_rows']
110	
111	
112	def compare_with_archive(new):
113	    old = json.loads((SNAP / 'results.json').read_text())
114	    out = {}
115	    for name in NAMES:
116	        o = {(r['x'], r['ratio_target']): r for r in all_rows(old, name)}
117	        n = {(r['x'], r['ratio_target']): r for r in all_rows(new, name)}
118	        if set(o) != set(n):
119	            raise RuntimeError(f'row sets differ for {name}')
120	        exact = all(o[k]['sum_Q_squared_weighted'] == n[k]['sum_Q_squared_weighted']
121	                    and o[k]['y'] == n[k]['y'] for k in o)
122	        dv = max(abs(Decimal(o[k]['V_decimal']) / Decimal(n[k]['V_decimal']) - 1) for k in o)
123	        po, pn = old['polynomials'][name], new['polynomials'][name]
124	        ce_o, ce_n = po['constant_extrapolated'], pn['constant_extrapolated']
125	        out[name] = dict(rows=len(o), integer_counts_identical=exact,
126	                         max_relative_difference_V=float(dv),
127	                         extrapolated_constant_difference=abs(ce_o['value'] - ce_n['value']),
128	                         envelope_difference=abs(ce_o['uncertainty'] - ce_n['uncertainty']),
129	                         fixed_ratio_slope_difference=abs(po['fit_fixed_ratio']['alpha_plus_beta']
130	                                                          - pn['fit_fixed_ratio']['alpha_plus_beta']))
131	    return out
132	
133	
134	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
135	# 2. Arithmetic helpers
136	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
137	
138	def primes_upto(n):
139	    s = np.ones(n + 1, dtype=bool)
140	    s[:2] = False
141	    for p in range(2, math.isqrt(n) + 1):
142	        if s[p]:
143	            s[p * p::p] = False
144	    return np.nonzero(s)[0]
145	
146	
147	def powmod_vec(base, exp, mod):
148	    """Elementwise base**exp % mod for int64 arrays with mod < 3e9."""
149	    base = base % mod
150	    result = np.ones_like(mod)
151	    exp = exp.copy()
152	    while np.any(exp > 0):
153	        odd = (exp & 1) == 1
154	        result = np.where(odd, (result * base) % mod, result)
155	        base = (base * base) % mod
156	        exp >>= 1
157	    return result
158	
159	
160	def rho_formula(name, P):
161	    """(rho(p), rho(p^2)) for each prime in P, from the closed forms listed in
162	    Section 10.2.  They are checked against brute force by rho_bruteforce_check."""
163	    P = P.astype(np.int64)
164	    if name == 'k^2+1':
165	        r1 = np.where(P == 2, 1, np.where(P % 4 == 1, 2, 0))
166	        r2 = np.where(P == 2, 0, r1)
167	    elif name == 'k^3+2':
168	        cube = powmod_vec(np.full_like(P, -2), (P - 1) // 3, P) == 1
169	        r1 = np.where((P == 2) | (P == 3) | (P % 3 == 2), 1, np.where(cube, 3, 0))
170	        r2 = np.where((P == 2) | (P == 3), 0, r1)
171	    elif name == '2k+1':
172	        r1 = np.where(P == 2, 0, 1)
173	        r2 = r1.copy()
174	    elif name == 't':
175	        r1 = np.ones_like(P)
176	        r2 = np.ones_like(P)
177	    return r1.astype(np.float64), r2.astype(np.float64)
178	
179	
180	def rho_bruteforce_check(name, bound=1000):
181	    f = POLY[name][0]
182	    P = primes_upto(bound)
183	    r1, r2 = rho_formula(name, P)
184	    for i, p in enumerate(P):
185	        p = int(p)
186	        for m, expect in [(p, r1[i]), (p * p, r2[i])]:
187	            a = np.arange(m, dtype=np.int64)
188	            val = f(a) % m if name != 'k^3+2' else ((a * a % m) * a + 2) % m
189	            if int(np.count_nonzero(val == 0)) != int(expect):
190	                raise RuntimeError(f'rho mismatch for {name} at {m}')
191	    return len(P)

194	def local_factors(p):
195	    p = p.astype(np.float64)
196	    a_m1 = -3 / p ** 2 + 2 / p ** 3                                  # a_p - 1
197	    ba = -1 / p + p ** -1.5 + p ** -2 - p ** -2.5                     # b_p - a_p
198	    cb = -p ** -1.5 * (1 - p ** -0.5) * (1 - 1 / p)                  # c_p - b_p
199	    return a_m1, ba, cb

202	def euler_constant(name, P):
203	    """Partial values (2/3) I prod_{p<=N} sigma_p and a rigorous interval for
204	    the full product (tail bound of Section 10.2)."""
205	    r1, r2 = rho_formula(name, P)
206	    xp, zp = r1 / P, r2 / (P.astype(np.float64) ** 2)
207	    a_m1, ba, cb = local_factors(P)
208	    s_m1 = a_m1 + ba * xp + cb * zp                                   # sigma_p - 1
209	    if np.any(1 + s_m1 <= 0):
210	        raise RuntimeError('nonpositive local factor')
211	    logs = np.log1p(s_m1)
212	    pref = 2 * float(I_CONST) / 3
213	    partial = {}
214	    for N in PRIME_CUTOFFS:
215	        partial[N] = pref * math.exp(math.fsum(logs[P <= N]))
216	    d = POLY[name][2]
217	    K = 3 + 2 * d
218	    N = PRIME_CUTOFFS[-1]
219	    # |log prod_{p>N} sigma_p| <= K/(1-K/N^2) * sum_{p>N} p^-2, and every prime
220	    # p > N >= 30 lies in one of 8 classes mod 30, each contributing at most
221	    # N^-2 + 1/(30N).
222	    tail = K / (1 - K / N ** 2) * 8 * (1 / N ** 2 + 1 / (30 * N))
223	    val = partial[N]
224	    return dict(partial=partial, value=val, lower=val * math.exp(-tail),
225	                upper=val * math.exp(tail), tail_log_bound=tail, K=K)

228	def vaughan_c2(P):
229	    """c_2 = 8 C_1 (-zeta(-1/2)) / (3 zeta(2)^2), Vaughan (2005), (1.14)-(1.15)
230	    with k = 2; C_1 truncated to p <= N."""
231	    p = P.astype(np.float64)
232	    term = ((p - 1) ** 2 * p ** 1.5 - 2 * p ** 4 + 3 * p ** 3 - p) / (p ** 2 * (p ** 2 - 1) ** 2)
233	    logs = np.log1p(term)
234	    pref = float(8 * (-mp.zeta(mp.mpf(-1) / 2)) / (3 * mp.zeta(2) ** 2))
235	    return {N: pref * math.exp(math.fsum(logs[P <= N])) for N in PRIME_CUTOFFS}

257	    """Longest decimal truncation shared by every number in [lower, upper]
258	    (0 < lower <= upper < 1); these digits are fixed by the interval."""

269	def euler_float_check(name, N=10 ** 5, dps=40):
270	    """Recompute (2/3) I prod_{p<=N} sigma_p with mpmath at dps digits, to
271	    gauge the floating-point rounding of euler_constant (not a certification)."""
272	    P = primes_upto(N)
273	    r1, r2 = rho_formula(name, P)
274	    with mp.workdps(dps):
275	        tot = mp.mpf(0)
276	        for p, a1, a2 in zip(P.tolist(), r1.tolist(), r2.tolist()):
277	            p = mp.mpf(p)
278	            a = 1 - 3 / p ** 2 + 2 / p ** 3
279	            b = (p - 1) * (p ** 2 - 2 + mp.sqrt(p)) / p ** 3
280	            c = (p - 1) ** 2 * (p + 1) / p ** 3
281	            xp, zp = mp.mpf(int(a1)) / p, mp.mpf(int(a2)) / p ** 2
282	            tot += mp.log(a * (1 - xp) + b * (xp - zp) + c * zp)
283	        return 2 * (-4 * mp.zeta(mp.mpf(-1) / 2)) / 3 * mp.exp(tot)

286	def eligibility(results, name):
287	    """For the rows at the largest x: the largest delta for which the row lies in
288	    the range x^(7/9+delta) <= f(y) <= x^(1-delta) of Theorem 1.1(iii), computed
289	    from the actual ratio f(y)/x (negative: outside the range for every delta)."""
290	    rows = all_rows(results, name)
291	    xl = max(r['x'] for r in rows)
292	    out = []
293	    for r in sorted([r for r in rows if r['x'] == xl], key=lambda r: r['ratio_target']):
294	        lr = math.log(r['fy']) / math.log(xl)
295	        out.append(dict(x=xl, ratio_target=r['ratio_target'], ratio_actual=r['ratio_actual'],
296	                        delta_max=min(lr - 7 / 9, 1 - lr)))

300	def symbolic_local_identity():
301	    p = sympy.symbols('p', positive=True)
302	    r = sympy.sqrt(p)
303	    a = 1 - 3 / p ** 2 + 2 / p ** 3
304	    b = (p - 1) * (p ** 2 - 2 + r) / p ** 3
305	    c = (p - 1) ** 2 * (p + 1) / p ** 3
306	    sig = a * (1 - 1 / p) + b * (1 / p - 1 / p ** 2) + c / p ** 2
307	    C1p = 1 + ((p - 1) ** 2 * p ** sympy.Rational(3, 2) - 2 * p ** 4 + 3 * p ** 3 - p) / (p ** 2 * (p ** 2 - 1) ** 2)
308	    checks = {
309	        'sigma_p(rho=1) == C_{1,p} (1-p^-2)^2': sympy.simplify(sig - C1p * (1 - p ** -2) ** 2) == 0,
310	        'a_p == (p-1)^2(p+2)/p^3': sympy.simplify(a - (p - 1) ** 2 * (p + 2) / p ** 3) == 0,
311	        'b_p - a_p == -1/p + p^-3/2 + p^-2 - p^-5/2': sympy.simplify(b - a - (-1 / p + p ** sympy.Rational(-3, 2) + p ** -2 - p ** sympy.Rational(-5, 2))) == 0,
312	        'c_p - b_p == -p^-3/2 (1-p^-1/2)(1-p^-1)': sympy.simplify(c - b + p ** sympy.Rational(-3, 2) * (1 - 1 / r) * (1 - 1 / p)) == 0,
313	        'zeta(-1/2) == -zeta(3/2)/(4 pi)': abs(mp.zeta(-0.5) + mp.zeta(1.5) / (4 * mp.pi)) < mp.mpf(10) ** -70,
314	    }
315	    if not all(checks.values()):
316	        raise RuntimeError(f'symbolic check failed: {checks}')
317	    return {k: bool(v) for k, v in checks.items()}

320	def A0_mp():
321	    """A_0 = prod_p (1 - 2/p^2) to ~40 digits."""
322	    P0 = 1000
323	    small = [int(p) for p in primes_upto(P0)]
324	    head = mp.fsum(mp.log(1 - mp.mpf(2) / p ** 2) for p in small)
325	    tail = mp.mpf(0)
326	    for k in range(1, 30):
327	        pz = mp.primezeta(2 * k) - mp.fsum(mp.mpf(p) ** (-2 * k) for p in small)
328	        tail -= mp.mpf(2) ** k / k * pz
329	    return mp.exp(head + tail)

332	def Ah_mp():
333	    """A_h = prod_p (1 - 3/p^2 + 2/p^3) to ~40 digits."""
334	    P0 = 1000
335	    small = [int(p) for p in primes_upto(P0)]
336	    head = mp.fsum(mp.log(1 - mp.mpf(3) / p ** 2 + mp.mpf(2) / p ** 3) for p in small)
337	    tail = mp.mpf(0)
338	    for k in range(2, 30):
339	        ck = -(2 + mp.mpf(-2) ** k) / k
340	        pz = mp.primezeta(k) - mp.fsum(mp.mpf(p) ** (-k) for p in small)
341	        tail += ck * pz
342	    return mp.exp(head + tail)

345	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
346	# 3. MT(x; q) and h(q)
347	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
348	
349	class Arithmetic:
350	    """eta(t) for t <= tmax and the constants entering MT and h."""
351	    TSTAR = 64     # head of the eta-sums evaluated in 80-digit arithmetic
352	
353	    def __init__(self, tmax):
354	        tmax = max(tmax, self.TSTAR + 1)
355	        self.tmax = tmax
356	        eta = np.ones(tmax + 1)
357	        eta[0] = 0.
358	        for p in primes_upto(tmax):
359	            p = int(p)
360	            eta[p::p] /= (p * p - 2)
361	            eta[p * p::p * p] = 0.
362	        self.eta = eta
363	        self.t = np.arange(tmax + 1, dtype=np.float64)
364	        self.kappa = eta * self.t ** 2
365	        self.eta_t2 = np.divide(eta, self.t ** 2, out=np.zeros_like(eta), where=self.t > 0)
366	        self.A0mp = A0_mp()
367	        self.A0 = float(self.A0mp)
368	        self.Ahmp = Ah_mp()
369	        self.head_cache = {}
370	        self.eta_mp = [mp.mpf(0)] + [mp.mpf(1) for _ in range(self.TSTAR)]
371	        for t in range(1, self.TSTAR + 1):
372	            fac = sympy.factorint(t)
373	            if any(e > 1 for e in fac.values()):
374	                self.eta_mp[t] = mp.mpf(0)
375	            else:
376	                self.eta_mp[t] = mp.fprod(mp.mpf(1) / (p * p - 2) for p in fac)
377	
378	    def heads(self, qprimes, th):
379	        """80-digit A_0 * sum_{t<=th,(t,q)=1} eta(t) and eta(t)/t^2."""
380	        small = tuple(p for p in qprimes if p <= self.TSTAR)
381	        key = (small, th)
382	        if key not in self.head_cache:
383	            s2 = s4 = mp.mpf(0)
384	            for t in range(1, th + 1):
385	                if self.eta_mp[t] and all(t % p for p in small):
386	                    s2 += self.eta_mp[t]
387	                    s4 += self.eta_mp[t] / t ** 2
388	            self.head_cache[key] = (self.A0mp * s2, self.A0mp * s4)
389	        return self.head_cache[key]
390	
391	    def MT(self, x, q, fac):
392	        """MT(x; q) for integer x, q with q <= x; fac = factorisation of q.
393	
394	        Uses the factorisation t = t0 t1 t2 of the proof of Proposition 6.2:
395	        for t0 > sqrt(Z),
396	        B(Z/t0^2) = Z/t0^2 - Z^2/t0^4, and the complete eta-sums over t0 coprime
397	        to q are known in closed form, so the infinite t0-sum is evaluated
398	        exactly up to rounding."""
399	        S1 = [p for p, e in fac.items() if e == 1]
400	        S2 = [p for p, e in fac.items() if e >= 2]
401	        qprimes = list(fac)
402	        E2 = math.prod(1 + 1 / (p * p - 2) for p in S2)
403	        full2 = SIX_PI2 * mp.fprod(mp.mpf(p * p - 2) / (p * p - 1) for p in qprimes)
404	        full4 = SIX_PI2 ** 2 * mp.fprod(mp.mpf(p * p) * (p * p - 2) / (p * p - 1) ** 2 for p in qprimes)
405	        Tmax = math.isqrt(x // q)
406	        if Tmax > self.tmax:
407	            raise RuntimeError('tmax too small')
408	        ts = np.arange(1, Tmax + 1)
409	        cop = (self.eta[1:Tmax + 1] > 0) & (np.gcd(ts, q) == 1)
410	        total = 0.
411	        for r in range(len(S1) + 1):
412	            for sub in itertools.combinations(S1, r):
413	                t1 = math.prod(sub)
414	                eta1 = math.prod(1 / (p * p - 2) for p in sub)
415	                Z = x / (q * t1)
416	                T = math.isqrt(x // (q * t1))
417	                if T >= 1:
418	                    u = Z / self.t[1:T + 1] ** 2
419	                    fr = u - np.floor(u)
420	                    SB = float(np.sum((self.kappa[1:T + 1] * fr * (1 - fr))[cop[:T]]))
421	                else:
422	                    SB = 0.
423	                th = min(T, self.TSTAR)
424	                h2, h4 = self.heads(qprimes, th)
425	                br2, br4 = float(full2 - h2), float(full4 - h4)
426	                if T > self.TSTAR:
427	                    m = cop[self.TSTAR:T]
428	                    br2 -= self.A0 * float(np.sum(self.eta[self.TSTAR + 1:T + 1][m]))
429	                    br4 -= self.A0 * float(np.sum(self.eta_t2[self.TSTAR + 1:T + 1][m]))
430	                total += eta1 * t1 * (self.A0 * SB + Z * br2 - Z * Z * br4)
431	        return q * E2 * total
432	
433	    def h(self, fac):
434	        """h(q) = I prod_{p not | q} a_p prod_{p||q} b_p prod_{p^2|q} c_p."""
435	        val = self.Ahmp * I_CONST
436	        for p, e in fac.items():
437	            p = mp.mpf(p)
438	            a = 1 - 3 / p ** 2 + 2 / p ** 3
439	            lam = (p - 1) * (p ** 2 - 2 + mp.sqrt(p)) / p ** 3 if e == 1 else (p - 1) ** 2 * (p + 1) / p ** 3
440	            val *= lam / a
441	        return float(val)
442	
443	
444	def factor_table(values):
445	    vmax = max(values)
446	    if vmax <= 2 * 10 ** 7:
447	        spf = np.zeros(vmax + 1, dtype=np.int32)
448	        for p in primes_upto(math.isqrt(vmax) + 1):
449	            p = int(p)
450	            blk = spf[p * p::p]
451	            blk[blk == 0] = p
452	        out = []
453	        for v in values:
454	            fac = {}
455	            while v > 1:
456	                p = int(spf[v]) or v
457	                while v % p == 0:
458	                    v //= p
459	                    fac[p] = fac.get(p, 0) + 1
460	            out.append(fac)
461	        return out
462	    return [{int(p): int(e) for p, e in sympy.factorint(v).items()} for v in values]
463	
464	
465	def identity_selftest(ar):
466	    """Check the exact identity of Proposition 4.1 (P2) at x = 3000 for
467	    q <= 40, with every term computed by brute force except MT, which uses
468	    Arithmetic.MT.  Returns the largest relative discrepancy."""
469	    x = 3000
470	    sf = np.ones(x + 1, dtype=np.int64)
471	    sf[0] = 0
472	    for d in range(2, math.isqrt(x) + 1):
473	        sf[d * d::d * d] = 0
474	    c6 = float(SIX_PI2)
475	    Qx = int(sf.sum())
476	    worst = 0.
477	    for q in range(1, 41):
478	        fac = {int(p): int(e) for p, e in sympy.factorint(q).items()}
479	        g = np.empty(q)
480	        for l in range(q):
481	            v = c6 / q * math.prod(1 / (1 - p ** -2) for p in fac)
482	            for p, e in fac.items():
483	                if e == 1 and l % p == 0:
484	                    v *= 1 - 1 / p
485	                if e >= 2 and l % (p * p) == 0:
486	                    v = 0.
487	            g[l] = v
488	        n = np.arange(1, x + 1)
489	        counts = np.bincount(n % q, weights=sf[1:], minlength=q)
490	        E = counts - g * x
491	        V = float(np.sum(E ** 2))
492	        Dsum = 0.
493	        for hh in range(1, x // q + 1):
494	            m = hh * q
495	            C = int(np.sum(sf[1:x - m + 1] * sf[1 + m:x + 1]))
496	            A = ar.A0 * sum(ar.eta[t] for t in range(1, math.isqrt(m) + 1) if m % (t * t) == 0)
497	            Dsum += C - A * (x - m)
498	        rhs_wo_MT = 2 * Dsum + (Qx - c6 * x) - 2 * x * float(np.sum(g * E))
499	        mt = ar.MT(x, q, fac)
500	        worst = max(worst, abs(V - (mt + rhs_wo_MT)) / max(1., abs(V)))
501	    return worst
502

504	def shape_rows(results, ar):
505	    """For selected rows: V (snapshot), sum f'(k) MT(x;f(k)) and sum F(k) h(f(k))."""
506	    out = []
507	    for name in NAMES:
508	        f, fp, _ = POLY[name]
509	        rows = all_rows(results, name)
510	        for x in SHAPE_XS[name]:
511	            rr = sorted([r for r in rows if r['x'] == x], key=lambda r: r['y'])
512	            ymax = rr[-1]['y']
513	            qs = [f(k) for k in range(1, ymax + 1)]
514	            facs = factor_table(qs)
515	            mt = np.array([fp(k) * ar.MT(x, q, fa) for k, q, fa in zip(range(1, ymax + 1), qs, facs)])
516	            hf = np.array([fp(k) * math.sqrt(q) * ar.h(fa) for k, q, fa in zip(range(1, ymax + 1), qs, facs)])
517	            cmt, ch = np.cumsum(mt), np.cumsum(hf)
518	            for r in rr:
519	                y, Y = r['y'], r['fy']
520	                V = float(Decimal(r['V_decimal']))
521	                norm = math.sqrt(x) * Y ** 1.5
522	                out.append(dict(poly=name, x=x, ratio_target=r['ratio_target'], ratio_actual=r['ratio_actual'],
523	                                y=y, N_data=V / norm, N_MT=float(cmt[y - 1]) / norm,
524	                                V_over_sumMT=V / float(cmt[y - 1]), N_h=float(ch[y - 1]) / Y ** 1.5))
525	    return out

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Regenerate every number in the manuscript's numerical tables and plots.

Invoke from the workspace root:

    python3 manuscript/reproduce.py

What it does (details in manuscript/README.md):

1. Copies the accepted snapshot's ``compute.py`` and ``counts.cpp`` from
   ``source/numerics/snapshot`` into a scratch work directory (after checking
   their SHA-256 against ``source/numerics/accepted.json``) and runs
   ``compute.py`` there unchanged.  That script compiles ``counts.cpp`` with
   clang++, re-runs its validations, recomputes V_f(x, y) on the full grid
   x = 2.5e5, ..., 2.56e8, and redoes the empirical fits.  The archived
   executable is not used.
2. Compares the regenerated ``results.json`` with the archived one.
3. Computes, with code in this file, the quantities of the theorem that are
   not part of the snapshot: the constant C_f (Euler product over p <= 1e7,
   with a rigorous bound for the omitted primes), Vaughan's constant c_2,
   the sums  sum_k f'(k) MT(x; f(k))  and  sum_k F(k) h(f(k))  at selected rows,
   and a self-test of the exact identity of Proposition 4.1 (P2).
4. Writes LaTeX table fragments and PGFPlots data files to
   ``manuscript/generated/`` and the index ``manuscript/reproduction.json``.

No value is copied from proof prose or from the archived results; the
archived ``results.json`` is read only for the agreement check in step 2.
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import itertools
import json
import math
import pathlib
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_CEILING, ROUND_FLOOR

import numpy as np
import mpmath as mp
import sympy

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
WS = HERE.parent
SNAP = WS / 'source' / 'numerics' / 'snapshot'
ACCEPTED = WS / 'source' / 'numerics' / 'accepted.json'
GEN = HERE / 'generated'
DEFAULT_WORK = WS / 'scratch' / 'reproduce-work'
MARKER = '.reproduce-work'

NAMES = ['k^2+1', 'k^3+2', '2k+1']
TEXNAME = {'k^2+1': '$k^2+1$', 'k^3+2': '$k^3+2$', '2k+1': '$2k+1$', 't': '$t$ (formal)'}
POLY = {'k^2+1': (lambda k: k * k + 1, lambda k: 2 * k, 2),
        'k^3+2': (lambda k: k ** 3 + 2, lambda k: 3 * k * k, 3),
        '2k+1': (lambda k: 2 * k + 1, lambda k: 2, 1),
        't': (lambda k: k, lambda k: 1, 1)}
RATIOS = [.01, .02, .05, .1, .2, .4, .7, 1.]
PRIME_CUTOFFS = [10 ** 3, 10 ** 4, 10 ** 5, 10 ** 6, 10 ** 7]
# Rows of the exact-shape comparison (Table 5).  The linear polynomial has
# about x/2 moduli, so it is restricted to the two smallest sizes.
SHAPE_XS = {'k^2+1': [1000000, 16000000, 256000000],
            'k^3+2': [1000000, 16000000, 256000000],
            '2k+1': [250000, 1000000]}

mp.mp.dps = 80
I_CONST = -4 * mp.zeta(mp.mpf(-1) / 2)          # I = -4 zeta(-1/2)
SIX_PI2 = 6 / mp.pi ** 2


def sha256(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(pathlib.Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()

# 1. Snapshot re-run
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def run_snapshot(work, reuse):
    accepted = json.loads(ACCEPTED.read_text())['artifacts']
    for name in ['compute.py', 'counts.cpp']:
        if sha256(SNAP / name) != accepted[name]:
            raise RuntimeError(f'{name} does not match the accepted snapshot hash')
    elapsed = None
    if not (reuse and (work / 'results.json').exists()):
        if work.exists():
            # Only ever delete a directory that this script created itself.
            if any(work.iterdir()) and not (work / MARKER).exists():
                raise RuntimeError(f'{work} is not empty and was not created by reproduce.py; '
                                   'choose another --work directory')
            shutil.rmtree(work)
        work.mkdir(parents=True)
        (work / MARKER).write_text('scratch directory of manuscript/reproduce.py; safe to delete\n')
        for name in ['compute.py', 'counts.cpp']:
            shutil.copy2(SNAP / name, work / name)
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(work / 'compute.py')], cwd=work, check=True)
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - t0
    for name in ['compute.py', 'counts.cpp']:
        if sha256(work / name) != accepted[name]:
            raise RuntimeError(f'work copy of {name} differs from the snapshot')
    results = json.loads((work / 'results.json').read_text())
    return results, elapsed


def all_rows(res, name):
    p = res['polynomials'][name]
    return p['rows'] + p['diagnostic_rows']


def compare_with_archive(new):
    old = json.loads((SNAP / 'results.json').read_text())
    out = {}
    for name in NAMES:
        o = {(r['x'], r['ratio_target']): r for r in all_rows(old, name)}
        n = {(r['x'], r['ratio_target']): r for r in all_rows(new, name)}
        if set(o) != set(n):
            raise RuntimeError(f'row sets differ for {name}')
        exact = all(o[k]['sum_Q_squared_weighted'] == n[k]['sum_Q_squared_weighted']
                    and o[k]['y'] == n[k]['y'] for k in o)
        dv = max(abs(Decimal(o[k]['V_decimal']) / Decimal(n[k]['V_decimal']) - 1) for k in o)
        po, pn = old['polynomials'][name], new['polynomials'][name]
        ce_o, ce_n = po['constant_extrapolated'], pn['constant_extrapolated']
        out[name] = dict(rows=len(o), integer_counts_identical=exact,
                         max_relative_difference_V=float(dv),
                         extrapolated_constant_difference=abs(ce_o['value'] - ce_n['value']),
                         envelope_difference=abs(ce_o['uncertainty'] - ce_n['uncertainty']),
                         fixed_ratio_slope_difference=abs(po['fit_fixed_ratio']['alpha_plus_beta']
                                                          - pn['fit_fixed_ratio']['alpha_plus_beta']))
    return out
